# Image-guided SVG and 3D assets

## Workflow

1. Reuse a supplied reference when it serves the request. Otherwise, use the user's brief as the basis for the image-generation prompt, adding only constraints for asset isolation, readable construction, and the target medium. Avoid unrequested decorative extras; use a transparent background for cutouts and a plain background otherwise, unless the user requests a setting or it is part of the asset. Start with one image and inspect whether it meets the brief and has coherent forms and spatial relationships; check alpha when transparency matters. Use image generation to resolve errors or ambiguities in a generated reference that would affect construction, preserving unaffected design choices; inspect the revision before building. Keep additional views consistent with the accepted reference.
2. Create the editable asset from the reference. Match the silhouette, proportions, perspective, overlaps, and negative spaces before refining smaller features. Reproduce distinctive shapes, line weight, lighting, materials, and details with their placement and variation rather than substituting generic motifs. Before applying a method across repeated features or materials, render one representative part against the reference at intended and enlarged sizes; adjust the method until it preserves the distinctive appearance. Follow the user's requirements where the reference differs.
3. Render the asset and make a side-by-side comparison with the reference at matching scale and framing, including full views and close-ups. Identify the most visible mismatches in shape, placement, materials, highlights, and shadows; correct them, re-render, and compare again. If a key mismatch persists, refit or rebuild that part using another method and compare again. Repeat until no meaningful improvements can reasonably be made. For 3D, align the camera using reference landmarks, match lighting and reflected surroundings, and inspect other relevant angles for depth, connections, and geometry or material problems. Test a representative edit in the saved asset where practical.

## Medium-specific guidance

- **SVG:** Build the finished artwork from vector paths, shapes, and fills; do not embed the raster reference. For generated references, request clear contours and separable features for tracing; restrain incidental fine texture where appropriate while preserving the requested style, material appearance, and distinctive details. Use smooth curves for curved contours. When the requested style includes shading, preserve its major color transitions, dark accents, and highlights with multi-stop gradients and layered vector shapes. For intricate raster reference details, use a Python script with an available tracer such as VTracer to make a detailed trace as a fidelity baseline; if none is available, reconstruct those details and compare them with the reference. Inspect the trace; reconstruct parts or combine methods where this improves fidelity or meets editing requirements. Favor the best reference match even with many paths or less convenient grouping, while honoring any specific output or editing requirements. Tune color precision, detail, curve fitting, and noise removal to the reference; if shading or detail still suffers, compare another available tracing method. Retain the detailed version before cleanup. If a trace looks stepped, compare a trace made from higher-resolution or interpolated input and refit affected contours as needed. If a trace loses needed transparency, try a separate vector alpha mask on the color trace. Refit rough contours and repair fragmented traces while preserving color, shading, distinctive detail, and material depth; group parts where practical. Maintain continuous coverage for intended solid regions; selectively overlap or back adjoining shapes to prevent gaps, preserving intended transparency, cutouts, and open strokes. Give standalone SVGs a suitable `viewBox`; render at small and large sizes and intended aspect ratios, including in the intended viewer when practical. Inspect contours and joins up close on contrasting backgrounds, temporarily hiding a removable canvas if needed. When testing transparency, scan the alpha render at useful thresholds for enclosed transparent or partially transparent gaps using [scripts/review_alpha.py](scripts/review_alpha.py) or an equivalent check; compare candidates to the reference before fixing unintended gaps, seams, halos, and jagged edges. Check that IDs are unique and internal references resolve.
- **3D:** When no 3D tool or workflow is specified, prefer Blender if it is available. Build editable geometry and materials, inferring unseen geometry where needed. Give volumetric parts real depth and coherent connections. Match material texture scale and variation to the reference. If exporting, bake unsupported procedural material effects when they matter to the appearance, then inspect geometry and materials in the exported format. If using a shaded reference as a projected texture, check other angles and changed lighting for stretching and baked-in shading.
